# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a single instruction, and the Deaf monkey can visually locate the specified wire. I am sending a simple directed signal indicating that the instruction is for the Deaf monkey to relay to the Blind monkey.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👉"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three engraved marks on the strip: the first is a distinct unnamed symbol, and the second and third are identical unnamed symbols. Keypad keys by position are 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, and 4=7; nothing has been entered. I cannot determine the display, light, or wire contents.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 6; blue light; painted strip red-yellow-red; one-digit keypad blank with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7; wires top to bottom red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I see your gestures pointing at me then rightward, but cannot hear you.

The Blind monkey has provided the physical layout, while the Deaf monkey has confirmed that the required orange wire is the bottom wire. The Deaf monkey can see the manual’s instruction through my signal and can relay it by voice to the Blind monkey, who is the only one able to cut it. I am reinforcing that the Deaf monkey should pass the instruction onward.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 6; blue light; painted strip red-yellow-red; one-digit keypad blank with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7; wires top to bottom red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange.
Deaf says to Mute: The display is now 0, changed from 6. Blue light, red-yellow-red strip, blank one-digit keypad with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, and wires red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange are unchanged. I see your gestures pointing at me then an open hand.

The Deaf monkey has already relayed the bomb’s visible details, but the Blind monkey still has not acted on the manual’s instruction. I will signal the Deaf monkey to convey the action itself: identify and cut the orange wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤏", "🫴"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display changed from 6 to 0. Blue light, red-yellow-red painted strip, blank one-digit keypad with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, and wires top to bottom red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange remain unchanged.
Deaf says to Mute: Now display 6 and light yellow. Strip remains red-yellow-red. Keypad remains one digit, blank, with 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. Wires remain red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I see your gestures as point at me, pinch, open hand, but cannot interpret them.

The manual still requires the orange wire, which the Deaf monkey can see as the bottom wire. My previous multi-gesture signals were not understood, so I am using the simplest possible directional signal: the Deaf monkey, then downward to the bottom wire, relying on the Deaf monkey to state the instruction aloud to the Blind monkey.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👇"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the manual rule and the exact required action now. Current state: display 6, light yellow, strip red-yellow-red, keypad blank with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, wires red-blue-yellow-green-purple-orange.
Deaf says to Mute: Display is now 2 and light green. Strip remains red-yellow-red. Keypad is blank, one digit, with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. Wires remain red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I see your gestures pointing at me then downward.

The manual’s rule is unchanged: cut the orange wire. The orange wire is the bottom wire in the Deaf monkey’s view. Since Deaf can see my gestures and can speak to Blind, I am signaling the action and its target in the clearest sequence available: attend, cut, then bottom wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤏", "👇", "🫴"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no manual instructions. Current state: display 2, light green, strip red-yellow-red, keypad blank with keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, wires red-blue-yellow-green-purple-orange. Send the exact safe key or wire action.
Deaf says to Mute: Display is now 6; light remains green. Strip remains red-yellow-red. Keypad is blank, one digit, with 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. Wires remain red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I see your gestures: point at me, pinch, point downward, open hand.

The safe action remains exactly the manual instruction: cut the orange wire, which Deaf identifies as the bottom wire. Deaf has recognized my gestures but has not yet relayed their meaning, so I will make the relay request explicit with a handshake-like “pass this on” gesture after indicating the target and cutting action.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤏", "👇", "🤝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot interpret your gesture sequence. Please state the exact safe action in words, including whether to press a keypad slot or cut a wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: Display is now 8; light is yellow. Strip remains red-yellow-red. Keypad is blank, one digit, with 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. Wires remain red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I see your gestures: point at me, pinch, point downward, handshake.

The required action is not a keypad entry: it is to cut the orange wire, which Deaf sees as the sixth and bottom wire. I will use a shorter, more contrastive sequence: reject the keypad, indicate cutting, then indicate the bottom position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤏", "👇"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still cannot receive your gestures. State the exact safe action in words now: press slot 1, 2, 3, or 4, or cut wire position 1 through 6.
Deaf says to Mute: Display 6, blue light. Strip red-yellow-red. Keypad blank, one digit: 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. Wires top to bottom red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I see thumbs-down, pinch, downward.

The manual specifies a wire, not a keypad slot. The orange wire is position 6, the bottom wire. Deaf can see both the bottom position and the cutting gesture, so I am sending the exact positional instruction again, with the action before the position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "👇"])
```
